source_bias_notes: Vendor-sponsored Total Economic Impact studies routinely report inflated theoretical ROIs by valuing reclaimed employee minutes at full hourly wages without proving actual balance-sheet cost removal.
Management consulting reports consistently frame operational bottlenecks as people and organizational redesign challenges to market high-margin business transformation advisory services.
Data security and DSPM vendors heavily oversample unmanaged SaaS file exposures and shadow AI stats to justify urgent software acquisitions.
Regulatory agencies and industry standard bodies emphasize mandatory compliance and legal liability over technology innovation to maintain strict consumer protection enforcement.
synthesis.change_since_last_run: The updated evidence reveals a widening divergence between copilot deployments, which are increasingly blocked by tenant permission overexposure and post-launch engagement fatigue, and autonomous back-office workflow agents, which are delivering proven double-digit P&L efficiencies. Regulatory scrutiny has intensified from consumer protection agencies against unmonitored automated servicing and debt-collection workflows. Operating model redesign and confidence-threshold human escalation have emerged as the primary differentiators of scaled enterprise implementations.
open_questions: At what point will software vendors shift from per-seat copilot licensing models to outcome-based or consumption-based pricing as enterprise seat renewals face ROI scrutiny?

How will financial and healthcare regulators enforce algorithmic explainability standards when autonomous multi-agent swarms execute non-deterministic actions across heterogeneous enterprise software estates?
Can enterprises successfully sanitize decades of defective SharePoint and cloud permission hygiene quickly enough to unlock safe enterprise-wide copilot grounding?
